attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Mother concerned about abnormal walking and slow developmental progress; wide-based waddling gait and reluctance to bear weight

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He began crawling at 10 months and has only recently started attempting to stand, though he frequently cries and appears uncomfortable bearing weight. His gait is wide-based and waddling.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Vitamin D deficiency
- Nutritional rickets

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 2000 units orally once daily
- Calcium carbonate 250 mg elemental calcium orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy
- Older sibling with history of nutritional rickets

SOCIAL HISTORY:
The family lives in northern Minnesota, and the child is exclusively breastfed without vitamin supplementation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical exam, his forehead appears prominent and rounded, and gentle pressure to the posterior skull bones causes a soft indentation that rebounds after release. There are palpable nodular enlargements at the junctions of the ribs and sternum, and his wrists appear widened. His legs show noticeable bowing when he attempts to stand.

IMAGING:
Radiographs of the wrists show metaphyseal cupping, fraying, and splaying.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden onset coughing and wheezing after choking on peanuts while playing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 3-year-old male with nutritional rickets diagnosed one year ago who is brought to the emergency department after suddenly developing coughing and wheezing while eating a handful of peanuts. His mother reports he was playing and running around when he started choking.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Nutritional rickets (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Vitamin D deficiency

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 2000 units orally once daily
- Calcium carbonate 250 mg elemental calcium orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal vitamin D deficiency during pregnancy
- Older sibling with history of nutritional rickets

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: None (Toddler).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On exam, he is in mild respiratory distress.
